prose.summary: VDC managers use digital models and coordination workflows to plan how construction will be delivered. They connect BIM, field sequencing, trade coordination and project management. The role is closer to construction execution than a BIM manager's broader model governance.
prose.day_to_day: The work can include coordination planning, model review, clash resolution and translating project information for construction teams. Managers align designers, trades and project staff around what must be resolved before work reaches the site. PivotHop does not currently have a job sample for this title, so employer practices are not measured.
prose.work_environment: VDC work is tied to active projects, coordination meetings and construction delivery. Some model tasks are computer-based, but field context and trade collaboration limit a purely remote view. Without a current job sample, no broader remote-work claim is justified.
prose.getting_in: Build substantial BIM and project-coordination experience, then show how a model changed a construction decision. Learn to run clash workflows, assign issues and verify resolution with the people installing the work. BIM managers and construction coordinators have the clearest adjacent foundation.
prose.ladder: Early VDC staff coordinate a discipline or contained project area. Responsibility grows toward projectwide planning, trade strategy, standards and leadership across several projects. The path can branch into BIM management, construction management or digital delivery.
prose.suits: This work fits people who enjoy models but judge them by whether construction becomes clearer. It requires comfort with site pressure, incomplete information and negotiation across trades. It is a poor fit if visual model quality matters more than installation reality.
prose.misconceptions: VDC is not simply BIM with a construction label. Its value comes from using models to resolve sequencing, access and coordination before the field pays for the conflict.
prose.who_qualifies: BIM managers, coordinators, construction managers and technically strong trade staff bring adjacent foundations. They need proof of issue ownership and construction decisions, not only model production. Current job data is unavailable to rank these routes further.
prose.what_the_numbers_miss: No current job sample is available to measure tools or employer patterns. A sample still would not show whether field leaders trust model-based coordination enough to act on it.

steps.how: Understand how design and trade models are created before trying to coordinate their conflicts.
Group issues, assign owners, record decisions and verify that the resolution is constructible.
Show how sequencing, access or installation changed because of the coordination work.
Explain the avoided conflict or clearer decision without inventing a financial saving.

prose.tools: BIM, Revit, MEP, project management, Navisworks and construction administration appear in adjacent route evidence. Current job data is unavailable for a stronger tool ranking.

pros: The work can prevent coordination problems before installation.
It combines digital models with practical construction decisions.
cons: Coordination decisions may arrive after trades have already planned the work.
Project pressure can favor quick fixes over durable coordination standards.

faq.q: how do you become a VDC manager?
faq.a: Build BIM and construction-coordination experience, then prove that your model work changed a field decision. Show issue ownership from clash through verified resolution.

faq.q: can a BIM manager move into VDC?
faq.a: Yes. BIM standards and coordination transfer, but the role requires stronger construction sequencing, trade and field-delivery evidence.

faq.q: what is the difference between VDC and BIM management?
faq.a: VDC focuses on using digital models for construction planning and delivery, while BIM management governs model standards and information across design or construction teams.
